key_insight: Egocentric human video can be a better pretraining source than scarce real-robot trajectories for embodied models. The core takeaway is that large-scale human first-person video provides richer diversity and better scaling potential while preserving useful embodied signals.
problem_solved: This paper tackles the data bottleneck in embodied foundation model pretraining. Real-robot teleoperation data is accurate but expensive, slow to collect, and limited in variety, making it hard to scale embodied learning.
method: Compare egocentric human video against teleoperated real-robot data as pretraining sources for embodied models.
Leverage human first-person video to provide scalable, diverse interaction and environment coverage.
Evaluate whether human video can transfer useful embodied priors and outperform robot-only pretraining.
impact: For AI/ML practitioners, this suggests a cheaper and more scalable path to build stronger embodied models without relying solely on costly robot data. It could significantly reduce data collection burden while improving generalization across tasks and environments.

paper_title: HumanScale: Egocentric Human Video Can Outperform Real-Robot Data for Embodied Pretraining
paper_authors: Juncheng Ma, Jianxin Bi, Yufan Deng, Xuanran Zhai, Kewei Zhang
